records.source: וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל דָּוִיד֩ וְשָׂרֵ֨י הַצָּבָ֜א לַעֲבֹדָ֗ה לִבְנֵ֤י אָסָף֙ וְהֵימָ֣ן וִֽידוּת֔וּן הַֽנִּבְּאִ֛יםבְּכִנֹּר֥וֹת בִּנְבָלִ֖ים וּבִמְצִלְתָּ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֥י מְלָאכָ֖ה לַעֲבֹדָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And set apart David and [the] commanders of the army for the service the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the prophesying with lyres, with harps and with cymbals; and was their number, men of work for their service:
pieces: David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals. This is the list of the men who did the work of their service:

L.1: And David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, with harps and with cymbals. And their number, [the] men of work for their service, was:

R.1: David and the army commanders set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for special service. Their work was to prophesy with music as they played lyres, harps and cymbals. Here is a list of the men who did this work:

decisions.choice: the commanders of the army: the leaders of the army, or possibly the leaders of the service
decisions.reason: The words are the usual title for army commanders (1 Chronicles 27:3; 2 Samuel 24:2), and leaders of the army may have shared in a national act like this one, as all the leaders of Israel did in 23:2. But the word for "army" is also used of the Levites' duty at the sanctuary (Numbers 4:3, 23; 8:24-25), so the phrase may here mean the leaders in charge of that service. The text does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: prophesied: spoke inspired words in worship, with music
decisions.reason: To prophesy is to speak as one moved by God. Here it is joined to instruments, and verse 3 explains it as giving thanks and praising the LORD. Music and prophecy go together elsewhere too (1 Samuel 10:5; 2 Kings 3:15). The singers' praise is presented as inspired speech, not only as skilled performance.

decisions.choice: lyres, harps and cymbals: the temple's string and percussion instruments
decisions.reason: The lyre and the harp were stringed instruments, the lyre the smaller; cymbals were struck metal plates. They are the instruments David assigned to the Levite musicians when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 13:8; 15:16).

decisions.choice: their number: the list that follows
decisions.reason: "Their number" introduces the names in verses 2-4 rather than a total; the total comes in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Their work was to prophesy with music as they played
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the prophesying was done through the music, as verse 3 says, and splits the sentence.

records.heading: The temple musicians

records.source: לִבְנֵ֣י אָסָ֗ף זַכּ֧וּר וְיוֹסֵ֛ף וּנְתַנְיָ֥ה וַאֲשַׂרְאֵ֖לָה בְּנֵ֣י אָסָ֑ף עַ֚ל יַד־אָסָ֔ף הַנִּבָּ֖א עַל־יְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: Of [the] sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, sons of Asaph, on [the] hand of Asaph the prophesying on [the] hands of the king.
pieces: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah. These sons of Asaph worked under Asaph's direction, and he prophesied at the king's direction.

L.2: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, [the] sons of Asaph, under [the] hand of Asaph, who prophesied under [the] hands of the king.

R.2: Asaph's sons were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah. Asaph led them, and he prophesied as the king directed.

decisions.choice: under the hand of: under the direction of
decisions.reason: "On the hand of" means under someone's charge or leadership. The sons worked under their father, and Asaph worked under the king, who had arranged the music for worship (verse 6; 1 Chronicles 6:16).

decisions.choice: who prophesied: Asaph himself
decisions.reason: The verb form is singular, so it describes Asaph, not his sons.

decisions.choice: under Asaph's direction, at the king's direction; led them, as the king directed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the picture "under the hand" in plain words.

records.source: לִידוּת֑וּן בְּנֵ֣י יְדוּת֡וּן גְּדַלְיָ֡הוּ וּצְרִ֡י וִֽ֠ישַׁעְיָהוּ חֲשַׁבְיָ֨הוּ וּמַתִּתְיָ֜הוּ שִׁשָּׁ֗ה עַל֩ יְדֵ֨י אֲבִיהֶ֤ם יְדוּתוּן֙ בַּכִּנּ֔וֹר הַנִּבָּ֕א עַל־הֹד֥וֹת וְהַלֵּ֖ל לַיהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Of Jeduthun: [the] sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six, on [the] hands of their father Jeduthun with the lyre, the prophesying in giving thanks and praising to Yahweh.
pieces: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six, under [the] hands of their father Jeduthun, with the lyre, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: Jeduthun's sons were Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six in all. Their father Jeduthun led them. He prophesied as he played the lyre, thanking and praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: six: one name is missing from the list
decisions.reason: The verse counts six sons but names five. Shimei, who receives the tenth lot with the sons of Jeduthun (verse 17), is probably the missing name; the old Greek translation includes Shimei here. With him, the twenty-four heads of verses 2-4 match the twenty-four lots of verses 9-31. The Hebrew text is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: prophesied in giving thanks and praising: inspired thanksgiving
decisions.reason: This defines what the musicians' prophesying was (verse 1): thanks and praise to the LORD, sung and played as speech moved by God.

decisions.choice: Zeri; Jeduthun
decisions.reason: Zeri is called Izri in verse 11. Jeduthun leads one of the three guilds of singers with Asaph and Heman (1 Chronicles 16:41-42); his name is in the titles of Psalms 39, 62 and 77.

decisions.choice: six in all
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the Hebrew count of six although only five names are listed; the footnote explains.

records.source: לְהֵימָ֑ן בְּנֵ֣י הֵימָ֡ן בֻּקִּיָּ֡הוּ מַתַּנְיָ֡הוּ עֻ֠זִּיאֵל שְׁבוּאֵ֨ל וִֽירִימ֜וֹת חֲנַנְיָ֣ה חֲנָ֗נִי אֱלִיאָ֤תָה גִדַּ֨לְתִּי֙ וְרֹמַ֣מְתִּי עֶ֔זֶר יָשְׁבְּקָ֣שָׁה מַלּ֔וֹתִי הוֹתִ֖יר מַחֲזִיאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Of Heman: [the] sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
pieces: Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth.

L.4: Of Heman: the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.

R.4: Heman's sons were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth.

decisions.choice: the last nine names: names, which may also form a line of poetry
alternatives: read the words as a line of poetry
decisions.reason: Read as ordinary words rather than names, the names from Hananiah to Mahazioth sound like a short prayer: roughly "Be gracious to me, Yah, be gracious to me; you are my God; I have magnified, and I have exalted help; sitting in hardship, I have spoken; give visions in plenty." Some forms would need small changes to read this way, and it is not known whether the names were given to fit a known psalm, whether a line of song was later read as names, or whether the likeness is chance. The verse presents them as the names of Heman's sons, and verses 23-31 use them as names, so they are kept as names.

decisions.choice: Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth
decisions.reason: In the lots these sons are called Azarel (verse 18), Shubael (verse 20) and Jeremoth (verse 22). The pairs are spelling or form variants of the same names, as Zeri and Izri are (verses 3, 11).

decisions.choice: Romamti-Ezer
decisions.reason: The name is written as two words in the Hebrew; it is given as one hyphenated name, as the source data spells it.

records.source: כָּל־אֵ֨לֶּה בָנִ֜ים לְהֵימָ֗ן חֹזֵ֥ה הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ בְּדִבְרֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לְהָרִ֣ים קָ֑רֶן וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לְהֵימָ֗ן בָּנִ֛ים אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר וּבָנ֥וֹת שָׁלֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: All these [were] sons of Heman, [the] seer of the king in [the] words of God, to lift up [a] horn; and gave God to Heman sons fourteen and daughters three.
pieces: All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer, in keeping with God's promises to lift up his horn; God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

L.5: All these [were] sons of Heman, the seer of the king in the words of God, to lift up [the] horn; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

R.5: All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer (a prophet who received messages from God). God had promised to make Heman strong and honored, and God gave him fourteen sons and three daughters.

decisions.choice: in the words of God, to lift up the horn: by God's promise to make Heman strong and honored
alternatives: the seer who spoke God's words to exalt the king
to raise praise, or sound the horn, in God's service
decisions.reason: An animal's horn is a picture of strength and honor, and "lifting up the horn" means giving someone strength and standing (1 Samuel 2:1, 10; Psalm 89:18, 25). The large family that follows seems to be how God kept that promise to Heman. The phrase could instead go with "seer" (Heman as the seer who spoke God's words to lift up the king's strength), or refer to raising praise, or even to sounding a horn in music. The reading taken links it to the gift of sons in the next clause.

decisions.choice: seer: a prophet who receives visions
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "see" and names someone who receives messages from God by vision. Gad is called David's seer with the same word (1 Chronicles 21:9). Heman is called the king's seer because he served David.

decisions.choice: fourteen sons and three daughters
decisions.reason: Many children were counted a mark of God's blessing (Psalm 127:3-5). The fourteen sons are those named in verse 4.

decisions.choice: his horn
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "his", taking the horn to be Heman's (see the footnote).

decisions.choice: the king's seer (a prophet who received messages from God); to make Heman strong and honored
decisions.reason: Readable explains "seer" once and gives the sense of the picture of the horn.

records.source: כָּל־אֵ֣לֶּה עַל־יְדֵי֩ אֲבִיהֶ֨ם בַּשִּׁ֜יר בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה בִּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ נְבָלִ֣ים וְכִנֹּר֔וֹת לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֚ל יְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְסאָסָ֥ף וִידוּת֖וּן וְהֵימָֽן׃
records.gloss: All these [were] on [the] hands of their father in the song [of the] house of Yahweh, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for [the] service of [the] house of the God, on [the] hands of the king, Asaph and Jeduthun and Heman.
pieces: All these were under their father's direction for the music in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with cymbals, harps and lyres, in the service of God's house. Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman served at the king's direction.

L.6: All these [were] under [the] hands of their father for the song [in the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for [the] service of the house of God, under [the] hands of the king: Asaph and Jeduthun and Heman.

R.6: All these men were led by their own fathers in making music in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They played cymbals, harps and lyres as part of the service in God's house. Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman took their directions from the king.

decisions.choice: their father: each son under his own father
decisions.reason: "All these" gathers the sons of all three families (verses 2-5), and each group worked under its own father: Asaph, Jeduthun or Heman.

decisions.choice: Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman: under the king's direction
decisions.reason: The three names at the end most likely go with "under the hands of the king": the fathers directed their sons, and the king directed the fathers (verse 2). They could also simply name the three fathers just mentioned, but the sense comes out the same.

decisions.choice: the song in the house of the LORD: music in temple worship
decisions.reason: Song here means the whole work of music, sung and played, in the worship of the sanctuary. The temple was not yet built; David was organizing its service in advance (1 Chronicles 22:5; 23:5).

decisions.choice: Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman served at the king's direction
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the three names the subject of a new sentence, following the reading in m2.

decisions.choice: their own fathers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that each son served under his own father.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י מִסְפָּרָם֙ עִם־אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם מְלֻמְּדֵי־שִׁ֖יר לַיהוָ֑ה כָּל־הַ֨מֵּבִ֔ין מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וּשְׁמוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was their number with their brothers, trained [in] song to Yahweh, all the understanding [ones], two hundred eighty and eight.
pieces: Their number, together with their relatives who were trained in singing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all of them skilled, was 288.

L.7: And their number with their brothers, trained [in] song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the skilled, was 288.

R.7: Together with their relatives, there were 288 men trained to sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all of them skilled musicians.

decisions.choice: brothers: relatives and fellow Levites
decisions.reason: The word "brothers" covers kinsmen in a wider sense than sons of the same parents: here the other Levites of the musicians' families who worked with them.

decisions.choice: trained in song; the skilled: taught and expert musicians
decisions.reason: The first word means "taught", the second "one who understands". Together they describe musicians who had learned their craft and were masters of it (compare 15:22, where Chenaniah directs the music "because he understood it").

decisions.choice: 288: twenty-four groups of twelve
decisions.reason: The number is twenty-four times twelve. Verses 9-31 divide the musicians into twenty-four groups of twelve, matching the twenty-four divisions of priests in chapter 24.

decisions.choice: brothers (Literal); relatives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable give its wider sense here. The same pattern is used in verses 9-31.

decisions.choice: 288 men; skilled musicians
decisions.reason: Readable adds "men" and "musicians" to make the count and the skill clear.

records.source: וַיַּפִּ֜ילוּ גּוֹרָל֣וֹת מִשְׁמֶ֗רֶת לְעֻמַּת֙ כַּקָּטֹ֣ן כַּגָּד֔וֹל מֵבִ֖ין עִם־תַּלְמִֽיד׃פ
records.gloss: And they cast lots [of] duty, corresponding, as the small as the great, understanding [one] with pupil.
pieces: They cast lots for their duties on equal terms, small and great alike, teacher and pupil alike.

L.8: And they cast lots [for] duty, side by side, as the small so the great, teacher with pupil.

R.8: They drew lots to decide the order of their duties. Everyone was treated the same, young and old, teacher and student.

decisions.choice: cast lots for duty: chose the order of service by lot
decisions.reason: Lots were drawn to leave a choice to God rather than to human favor (Proverbs 16:33). Here they set the order in which the twenty-four groups would take turns at the sanctuary, as the priests' turns were set in 24:5-19. The word for "duty" means a turn or watch of service.

decisions.choice: side by side, small and great alike: no one was given an advantage
decisions.reason: The phrase means on equal terms, as in 24:31. "Small and great" may mean young and old or lower and higher in rank; either way, all were treated alike.

decisions.choice: teacher with pupil
decisions.reason: The first word is the same as "the skilled" in verse 7: the master musician. The second, "pupil", is found only here in the Hebrew Bible and comes from the verb "learn".

decisions.choice: young and old
decisions.reason: Readable takes "small and great" as young and old, the most natural sense in a list of teachers and learners.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֧ל הָרִאשׁ֛וֹן לְאָסָ֖ף לְיוֹסֵ֑ף גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֽוּא־וְאֶחָ֥יו וּבָנָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: And went out the lot the first for Asaph to Joseph; Gedaliah the second, he and his brothers and his sons, two ten.
pieces: The first lot fell for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his relatives and his sons, twelve.

L.9: And the first lot went out for Asaph, to Joseph; Gedaliah the second, he and his brothers and his sons, twelve.

R.9: The first lot fell to Joseph, from Asaph's family. The second fell to Gedaliah, with his relatives and sons, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: the lot came out: the lot was drawn
decisions.reason: The lot "going out" means that it was drawn from a container or thrown down, naming who would serve in that turn (24:7; Numbers 33:54; Joshua 19:1).

decisions.choice: for Asaph to Joseph: Joseph, of Asaph's family
decisions.reason: "For Asaph" names the family, "to Joseph" the son who received the lot (verse 2). The other lots name only the son.

decisions.choice: Joseph's group: the count of twelve is not given
decisions.reason: Every other lot ends with "his sons and his brothers, twelve", but Joseph's has no such words. The words were probably lost in copying; the old Greek translation has them. Twenty-four groups of twelve make the 288 of verse 7, so Joseph's group was twelve too. The Hebrew is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: he and his brothers and his sons
decisions.reason: This first full entry names the leader himself with his group; the entries that follow say only "his sons and his brothers". Twelve is the size of each group, leader included.

decisions.choice: twelve men in all
decisions.reason: Readable adds "men" and "in all" to show that twelve is the size of each group. The same words are used in verses 10-31.

records.source: הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֣י זַכּ֔וּר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: The third Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, two ten.
pieces: The third to Zaccur, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

L.10: The third, Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

R.10: The third lot fell to Zaccur, with his sons and relatives, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: the third: the third lot fell to Zaccur
decisions.reason: The entries in verses 10-31 are short: the number of the lot, the leader's name, "his sons and his brothers", and the size of the group. "Lot" and "fell" are understood from verse 9. Zaccur is a son of Asaph (verse 2).

decisions.choice: The third to; The third lot fell to
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "to" from verse 9; Readable also repeats "lot fell". The same wording is used for every lot through verse 31.

records.source: הָרְבִיעִי֙ לַיִּצְרִ֔י בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: The fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, two ten.
pieces: The fourth to Izri, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

L.11: The fourth, to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

R.11: The fourth lot fell to Izri, with his sons and relatives, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: Izri: the Zeri of verse 3
decisions.reason: The son of Jeduthun called Zeri in verse 3 is called Izri here; the two forms differ by one letter and name the same man. The name is kept as each verse spells it.

records.source: הַחֲמִישִׁ֣י נְתַנְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: The fifth Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, two ten.
pieces: The fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

L.12: The fifth, Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

R.12: The fifth lot fell to Nethaniah, with his sons and relatives, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: the fifth lot: Nethaniah, a son of Asaph
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Nethaniah is a son of Asaph (verse 2).

records.source: הַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י בֻקִּיָּ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: The sixth Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, two ten.
pieces: The sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

L.13: The sixth, Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

R.13: The sixth lot fell to Bukkiah, with his sons and relatives, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: the sixth lot: Bukkiah, a son of Heman
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Bukkiah is the first-named son of Heman (verse 4).

records.source: הַשְּׁבִעִ֣י יְשַׂרְאֵ֔לָה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: The seventh Jesarelah, his sons and his brothers, two ten.
pieces: The seventh to Jesarelah, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

L.14: The seventh, Jesarelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

R.14: The seventh lot fell to Jesarelah, with his sons and relatives, twelve men in all.

decisions.choice: Jesarelah: the Asarelah of verse 2

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth lot: Romamti-Ezer, the last son of Heman
decisions.reason: As in verse 28. With this lot all the heads named in verses 2-4 (with Shimei, verse 17) have received a turn: four sons of Asaph, six of Jeduthun and fourteen of Heman, twenty-four groups of twelve, 288 musicians in all (verse 7). The lots began by alternating between the families and ended with Heman's many sons.

decisions.choice: Romamti-Ezer
decisions.reason: Written as two words in the Hebrew; given as one hyphenated name, as in verse 4.
